title: LELA: an LLM-based Entity Linking Approach with Zero-Shot Domain Adaptation

Classical entity linking approaches have not been applied to the acronym disambiguation task. Rather, the original paper proposed AcroBERT, a method that can be run both in a classical and in a zero-shot fashion. Since it outperformed alternative approaches by a wide margin (usually by a factor of two), we compare only to AcroBERT and the baselines in these categories. For the true zero shot group, we use GENRE De Cao et al. ( 2021b ) and the BLINK cross-encoder Wu et al. ( 2020 ) (not trained on the dataset). Table 3 shows that LELA outperforms all true zero-shot competitors by a huge margin of up to 54 percentage points. It also outperforms all other competitors, whether or not they were fine-tuned on the training data, on all domains except the biomedical one. LELA improves the best-reported macro-accuracy by 4.6 percentage points, and the scientific domain accuracy by 13.9 percentage points. ZELDA Milich and Akbik ( 2023 ) groups several established Wikipedia-based classical entity linking benchmarks. It aims at allowing for a fair comparison of supervised methods by mapping all mentions to the same Wikidata knowledge base and by providing a common Wikipedia-based train set and candidate dictionary to be used across all benchmarks and methods.
